content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I am working on a small project where I need to connect a 4-20mA signal to the I8 (0-10V) analog input of a [product_name]. Is it possible to use a 500 Ohm resistor to convert the current signal into a voltage signal for this input? Thank you for your assistance. [user_name].
Yes, a 500 Ohm resistor between the input and ground will convert the 4-20mA signal to a 2-10V voltage signal (note: it is not a full 0-10V range).
Please refer to this discussion for related information: [url]

Hello, the pressure sensor I’m using supplies a 4-20mA output powered at 24VDC, not 10VDC. As a result, the analog input register is showing its maximum value during online monitoring. I would appreciate any help with this issue. Regards, [user_name].
Hi [user_name], I hope you are using the same power supply for both the pressure transmitter and the [product_name], including sharing the same ground.

analysis.insight_summary: Users seek advice on interfacing a 4-20mA signal from a sensor with the analog voltage input of a [product_name] module. There is confusion regarding proper signal conversion and unexpected register readings indicating maximum value, likely caused by wiring or supply misconfiguration. The discussion highlights a lack of clear official documentation for common conversion scenarios, resulting in users having to troubleshoot through trial and error.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate a simple connection using a resistor to reliably convert a 4-20mA sensor output for an analog input, expecting that the input will read values accurately and not show constant maximum errors.
